note: Window agent p1850-p1859. keyframe_overrides/0-2: the Qing keyframes 1856, 1857 and 1859 leave Cliopatria's oversize Panthay shape (Kunming, east Yunnan, the Sichuan basin) and Wuchang to nobody; they now claim them (as p1860-p1869 does from 1860). keyframe_overrides/3: the Taiping 1856 keyframe stops holding Wuchang, which Qing forces retook in December 1856. keyframe_overrides/4-5: the umbrella british-colonial-empire row no longer takes New South Wales from its colony in 1856-1858. events/2: Egypt is the Sultan's vassal again for 1850-1859 (the relation closed whole in 1840 by an Ottoman vassal_end meant for the Levant; it runs on to the dossier's own vassal_end of 1865, so it shows in p1860-p1869 too). keyframe_overrides/6: the Raj keyframe of 1858 uses its 1859 outline, so about 410 cells of British India (Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand) are not left to nobody for the one year 1858. events/0-1: the Amur contest of 1858 is narrowed to the land the Qing held. rulings/0: the upper Rio Negro goes to Brazil in 1853.

region.text: the Amur's left bank and the Ussuri country, ceded or held jointly by the Aigun treaty

events.note: 28 May 1858: the Aigun dispute is redrawn over the land the Qing held, not the Okhotsk coast north of the Stanovoy. The gazetteer's Outer Manchuria takes in the whole of Khabarovsk krai, 1,714 cells north of the Qing's own 1857 shape that Russia held before 1858; events/1 opens the contest again over the Qing's land only. The Treaty of Nerchinsk page puts the old border 'along the east-west watershed through the Stanovoy Mountains and down the Uda River' 'to the Sea of Okhotsk' and says 'The control over the area between the Uda River and the mountain chain was left to be decided later'; that zone and the coast north of the watershed are Russian in the compiled map before 1858 (Cliopatria's Russian shape of 1857), so they are not drawn as newly contested in 1858. [Reviewer p1850-p1859, 2 Nov 2026: note corrected; it said the page names no Qing land beyond the line, but the page leaves the Uda zone undecided. The effect is unchanged.]

region.text: the Amur's left bank and the Ussuri country inside the Qing's own 1857 shape: the land the Aigun treaty ceded or put under joint rule (Amur Annexation: 'ceded all territories north of the Amur to Russia'; the area east of the Ussuri 'a Sino-Russian condominium'); the Qing refused to ratify

events.note: 28 May 1858: the Aigun contest is drawn over the Amur's left bank and the Ussuri country only. Same contest as qing-dynasty/ledger/51, limited to what the Qing held. The Amur Annexation page: the treaty 'ceded all territories north of the Amur to Russia', made the area east of the Ussuri and south of the Amur a condominium, and Beijing 'refused to ratify it'. The Nerchinsk page puts the old border on the Stanovoy watershed and down the Uda to the Sea of Okhotsk and leaves 'the area between the Uda River and the mountain chain' 'to be decided later'; the coast north of the watershed was not in dispute, and the Uda zone, drawn Russian before 1858, stays as it was. [Reviewer p1850-p1859, 2 Nov 2026: note corrected; the effect is unchanged.]

region.text: Egypt, Sinai and the Sudan under the pashas, as Cliopatria draws the dynasty in 1850

events.note: 1850: Egypt is drawn as the Sultan's vassal again. The History of Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty page: the firmans of 13 February 1841 'confined the pasha's authority to Egypt ... and to the Sudan', 'Various restrictions were laid upon Muhammad Ali, emphasizing his position as vassal', and 'The government of the pashalik of Egypt was made hereditary within the family of Muhammad Ali'. The relation opened in 1805 (this dossier's events/1 and ottoman-empire /ledger/159) was closed whole in November 1840 by ottoman-empire /ledger/186, which was meant for the Levant only, so Egypt was direct from 1840 to its own vassal_end of 1865; this opens it again for the whole window (p1840-p1849 may open it from 1841; a second opening merges). The page is silent on tribute under Abbas I and Said Pasha.

union.text: the part of Cliopatria's oversize Panthay shape of 1856 inside China: Kunming, east Yunnan, the Sichuan basin and the Guizhou and Chongqing edges, which the Qing held (the smaller Panthay state, cut to the Dali basin by its dossier, still wins its own cells by the size rule)

correction.text: the 1857 Qing shape plus the Qing part of the Panthay shape (Kunming, east Yunnan, Sichuan basin) plus Wuchang, retaken in December 1856

keyframe_overrides.why: The Panthay dossier cuts Cliopatria's Panthay shape (341,824 km2 for 1856-58, 408,545 km2 for 1859, reaching 31.6 N) to Dali and its surroundings, but the Qing keyframe, Cliopatria's own, leaves the whole oversize shape out, so about 1,300 cells (Kunming, east Yunnan, the Sichuan basin, parts of Guizhou and Chongqing) fall to nobody from 1856 on. The Panthay Rebellion page puts the rebels at Dali: 'by gaining control of Dali in 1856 (which they retained until its fall in 1872)', and says the go-betweens came from 'provinces which were not in rebellion, like Sichuan and Zhejiang'. It does not put Kunming, east Yunnan or Sichuan in rebel hands (Kunming was only 'attacked and sacked' on 'multiple occasions'), so that land stays Qing. Wuchang is added because the Taiping Rebellion page says 'In December 1856 Qing forces retook Wuchang for the final time'.

correction.text: the 1856 Taiping shape without Wuchang, retaken by Qing forces in December 1856

keyframe_overrides.why: The Taiping Rebellion page says 'In December 1856 Qing forces retook Wuchang for the final time'. The dossier's loss event of that month is undone by this keyframe, which keeps Wuchang for the whole of 1856 and so hands the land to nobody in 1857; the draft records each year's end, so Wuchang is Qing's at the end of 1856.

correction.text: the Raj of 1859 without Ceylon: Company India with the princely states (vassal tint by ledger) and Lower Burma; Kashmir and Jammu is a separate outline in these years; without the Khanate of Kalat, which was no part of British India before the 1876 treaty

keyframe_overrides.why: The Company rule in India page gives 'Nationalisation of the Company and assumption of direct administration by the British Crown: 1 November 1858'. The dossier's 1858 shape is only Cliopatria's 1858 British Empire outline and leaves the land that Cliopatria adds in 1859 (about 410 cells in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and elsewhere that the draft shows as nobody's through 1858) to nobody, because the princely states that have no dossier get no vassal event; the British Empire row's dissolve of 1 November then sweeps it to nobody for the year-end of 1858, and the 1859 keyframe snap hands it to the Raj. The land was under the Company until 31 October 1858 and the Crown from 1 November, so it is the Raj's at the end of 1858; this uses the 1859 outline (Raj without Ceylon and Kalat) for 1858 too.

region.text: the Brazilian province of Amazonas: the upper Rio Negro basin

rulings.why: Both dossiers' 1853 shapes put the upper Rio Negro with Brazil (Brazil's 1853 gain; New Granada's 1853 keyframe drops it), but the size rule gives the cells to the smaller New Granada in 1853 and its keyframe then sends them to nobody, leaving 741 cells of Amazonas a grey hole in every year from 1853. The Amazonas page: the comarca of Rio Negro was in the Empire from 1824, 'the Province of Amazonas was officially created by Emperor Pedro II in 1850' and São Gabriel on the upper Rio Negro had a fort from 1761. It gives no 1853 event and the page puts the settlement of the northern frontier in the 1908 Vasquez Cobo-Martins treaty, so this follows the dossiers' shape, not a treaty.
